# Twelve-point circle demonstration

Format version 1; generated by dev/build-explorer-demo.R from public dgraphs
constructors and grip::grip (edge_length metric, seed 17, 40 rounds and 80 final
rounds). The saved layout records the generating grip version. Coordinates are
12 equally spaced points on the unit circle in the xy plane. No input data were
collected from people; the numerical fixture and its recipe are by Pawel Gajer.

Both graphs are symmetric k-nearest-neighbor graphs with chord edge lengths,
without pruning or component repair. k=2 has 12 edges, k=4 has 24. The reference
distance is the shorter unit-circle arc between each pair of distinct points.
Relative RMS error means sqrt(mean((graph distance - reference)^2)) divided by
sqrt(mean(reference^2)), over the 66 unordered pairs. It is 0.01138407 for k=2
and 0.04127477 for k=4. Extra chords introduce shortcuts. Relative absolute
error q95 is the 95th percentile of abs(error)/reference; Pearson correlation
compares the two vectors of distances. The schema target 'surface' denotes the
analytic arc reference here, not an estimated fitted surface.

Saved GRIP layouts illustrate the graphs; appearance is not the error metric.
All asset paths are relative. Reading, relocating, or viewing this directory
requires no fitting and makes no writes here. To regenerate, run the recipe
from the repository with dgraphs build dependencies and grip installed.
